images.text:
Although it might sound like science fiction, the idea of replacing human body parts with machines is actually part of a science called bionics.

Bionics, in general, is the study of how the characteristics of living systems can be used to solve engineering problems. First, studies of how birds fly were used to improve airplane design. Then, scientists studied how the eye worked, so they could design better cameras.

Now, bionic scientists are studying how human body parts function. Of course they can use this information to design artificial parts to replace human ones.

In fact, bionics can be used very successfully in the area of artificial limbs. Clumsy prosthetic limbs are being replaced with artificial limbs that are electronically controlled. They work through electrical signals which are received from the muscles where the skin is in contact with the prosthesis.

Electrodes on the surface of the skin measure muscle movement and transfer that information to the bionic limb. Of course, these artificial limbs behave more like real ones. In fact, those who use one of these prostheses feel as if they have truly regained the use of a limb.

Of course, today, many body parts can be replaced by artificial ones. In fact, bionic scientists believe that one day, many more parts of the human body will be replaceable.

Discourse markers show how ideas are connected. They usually come at the beginning of a sentence.
Discourse markers can show a connection to what the speaker is saying and what was just said. They can also show what the speaker's opinion is about what is being said.

You can use modals to talk about degrees of certainty.

You use them to describe what is definite, probable, possible, or impossible from the speaker's point of view.
You can use must, may, might, and could to describe degrees of certainty.

Must = it's very likely
Must not / Could not / Can't = it's not possible
May / Might / Can / Could = it's possible
May not / Might not = it's possible this is not true
You use modal verbs to add meaning to other verbs. They come before the dictionary form (infinitive without to) of the main verb. Modal verbs can add meaning connected with certainty or obligation.

You can use modal verbs in the passive voice.
You use the passive voice when you want to focus on the "receiver" of the action, rather than the "doer" of the action.
